sig: both original terms and later amendments
1.cue: Data has TWO legit values → schema must hold both.

A.why: Patch after the fact — extraction is still broken underneath.

B.why: Fixes the root: schema now holds both values + effective date, so nothing is lost.

C.why: Deleting "superseded" text destroys info and adds a fragile pre-step.

D.why: Works sometimes, but throws away the original term — downstream may need both.

2.cue: Subagents are ISOLATED. The coordinator carries info between them.

A.why: Shared memory store isn't the standard pattern — subagents don't share state.

B.why: The coordinator receives output and puts it in the next agent's prompt. That IS the pattern.

C.why: Message queues = infra fantasy. Not how subagent orchestration works.

D.why: Subagents don't call each other directly — they're isolated.

3.cue: Synthesis can't see dates it was never given → make subagents pass dates.

A.why: Give the synthesis agent the missing ingredient: dates in structured output.

B.why: "Always treat newest as authoritative" — the word ALWAYS kills it. Older data isn't wrong here.

C.why: Auto-discarding data loses the growth story entirely — worse than the bug.

D.why: Only past 6 months = throwing away valid historical data.

sig: want to speak to someone who can actually help
4.cue: Frustrated + instantly fixable → acknowledge, offer BOTH paths.

A.why: Processing a refund they didn't confirm = acting without consent.

B.why: Honors the request, but skips telling them it's fixable RIGHT NOW.

C.why: More questions = more friction for someone already fed up.

D.why: Acknowledge feelings + "I can fix this now, or connect you to a person — your call."

sig: needs the DOI that `extract_metadata` would provide
5.cue: Force the FIRST call only — then let the rest flow in later turns.

A.why: Forcing it on EVERY call means enrichment tools can never run. Breaks the pipeline.

B.why: "any" + prompt hints = hoping, not guaranteeing. Soft fix for a hard ordering need.

C.why: Tool order in the array is NOT a priority signal. Myth answer.

D.why: Force extract_metadata first, then handle enrichment in following turns. Guaranteed order, nothing blocked.

6.cue: Do what you CAN, be honest about what you can't, offer paths.

A.why: Escalating wastes the work already done — most of the job IS finished.

B.why: Holding the customer hostage to a retry loop. "Keeping conversation open until success" = red flag.

C.why: Deliver the value you have, admit the system issue, offer escalate-or-retry. Balanced.

D.why: Promising a refund that never ran = lying to the customer.

7.cue: One shared past + two independent futures = fork_session.

A.why: Works, but a file summary loses the deep session context. Fork keeps everything.

B.why: Sequential in one session = strategy 2 gets contaminated by strategy 1.

C.why: fork_session: both branches inherit the full 23-file analysis, then diverge cleanly.

D.why: Re-reading everything twice = burning the expensive analysis you already paid for.

sig: fields not mentioned in the article
8.cue: Hallucinated fields → tell the model null is the right answer.

A.why: A second LLM to check the first = bolt-on cost for a prompt-level bug.

B.why: Making fields REQUIRED forces MORE guessing, not less. Backwards.

C.why: "Upgrade the model" is the lazy answer — the prompt never said null was okay.

D.why: One instruction: "return null if it's not in the source." Cheapest, targets the exact bug.

sig: sometimes kept as one entry, sometimes split
9.cue: THREE fuzzy judgment problems → few-shot examples show all three at once.

A.why: Adding confidence/quote metadata doesn't fix splitting or hallucinated skills.

B.why: "10-20 max" is an arbitrary cap — some docs really have 40 skills. Creates a new bug.

C.why: Examples demonstrate splitting, explicit-only, and granularity in one move. Fixes all three.

D.why: Post-hoc cleanup can't remove skills that were never stated (issue 2).

10.cue: Retry can't create information the model never saw.

A.why: Format/shape error — error feedback fixes this. Retry works.

B.why: The data is NOT in the input. No number of retries conjures it. Retry is useless here.

C.why: "1,234"→1234 is trivially fixable on retry.

D.why: Datetime→date is trivially fixable on retry.

11.cue: Trace the STRUCTURE (base class → interface → implementations), don't bulk-read.

A.why: 8K lines sequentially = context blown before understanding forms.

B.why: "Biggest files first" is arbitrary — size ≠ importance.

C.why: Follow the architecture: base class, interface, then the specific invalidation paths. Targeted + structural.

D.why: Grep-only with minimal context finds words, not understanding. Too shallow for "how it works".

12.cue: Vague tool contract → split into purpose-specific tools. (Structure > coaching.)

A.why: Pre-classifying still funnels into the same mushy free-text tool.

B.why: An enum mode helps, but output contracts are still undefined.

C.why: Better descriptions = coaching a vague interface. The marked answer — it's the bolt-on trap.

D.why: Purpose-specific tools with defined input/output contracts. Structural fix for a structural problem.

13.cue: Pass the draft + a structured claim→source index. Not everything, not nothing.

A.why: "Source names only" — citations need URLs/excerpts, not just names.

B.why: 138K tokens forwarded = context bomb. "Full accumulated context" is the extreme answer.

C.why: Post-hoc claim-matching is guesswork after the link is already lost.

D.why: Draft + structured source index mapping claims→URLs/excerpts. Exactly enough.

14.cue: You KNOW the name → --resume by name.

A.why: Re-reading = torching 2 hours of built context.

B.why: --continue grabs the MOST RECENT session — she's used 3 other codebases since. Wrong session.

C.why: --resume auth-deep-dive: load the exact named session. The stem literally hands you the name.

D.why: Would work, but hunting a UUID in transcript files when you have the name is pointless friction.

15.cue: Model can't RECOGNIZE varied formats → show it examples. Retry re-rolls the same blindness.

A.why: Few-shot across varied document structures teaches recognition — the actual skill gap.

B.why: The marked answer. Retry doesn't teach format recognition — same failure, more cost.

C.why: Regex populating fields the model missed = brittle shadow-extractor.

D.why: Making fields optional doesn't extract anything — it just legalizes the failure.

sig: teammate merged a PR that renamed two utility functions
16.cue: Small known change → resume + tell it what changed.

A.why: Silent staleness: agent will use the old function names.

B.why: Fresh agent + giant transcript pasted in = clunky, loses nothing-gains-nothing.

C.why: Safe but wasteful — a summary drops 47 files of detail over TWO renamed functions.

D.why: Resume the rich context, patch the two renames. Minimal loss, maximal accuracy.

17.cue: Same pattern as Q16: resume + inform which files changed.

A.why: The marked answer. Fresh start trashes an hour of context over a 25% file change.

B.why: Silent staleness again.

C.why: Resume + name the 3 changed files for targeted re-read. Efficiency AND accuracy.

D.why: Re-reading all 12 when 9 are unchanged = waste.

18.cue: Structured checkpoint reports > raw logs > vector search.

A.why: Semantic search to rebuild exact state = lossy and nondeterministic.

B.why: The marked answer. Full conversation log = high fidelity, terrible efficiency — the stem asked for BALANCE.

C.why: Each agent persists a structured report; coordinator injects what's relevant. Fidelity + efficiency.

D.why: Independent state files work but nobody coordinates what's relevant — coordinator is the right owner.

19.cue: Schema + normalization rules IN the prompt. One pass, source-level fix.

A.why: One call per field = cost explosion, loses cross-field context.

B.why: Post-processing works but pushes complexity downstream; model can normalize at the source.

C.why: Majority-vote extraction = paying 3-5x to dodge writing rules.

D.why: Strict schema + format rules in the prompt: normalize where the intelligence is.

20.cue: "Evolving distribution" kills static routers → let the coordinator decide per query.

A.why: The coordinator is already an LLM — let it route dynamically. Adapts as queries evolve.

B.why: Hard fast-path/full-path binary — middle-complexity queries get mis-routed.

C.why: Pattern rules go stale the moment users "discover new applications" (the stem warns you).

D.why: A trained classifier needs labels + retraining forever — heavyweight for what the coordinator does free.

21.cue: "Overall" is doing sneaky work — check the SEGMENTS before automating.

A.why: Threshold tuning matters, but AFTER you know accuracy holds per segment.

B.why: Pilot on live traffic before validating segments = shipping the risk to find the risk.

C.why: Aggregate 97% can hide a 70% document type (Simpson's paradox). Segment check is THE pre-automation gate.

D.why: Worth knowing, but doesn't validate the automation itself — and 97% aggregate may not hold everywhere.

sig: how does the agentic loop determine
22.cue: Agentic loop = results go in the conversation, the MODEL reasons. No trees, no scripts.

A.why: Fixed upfront plan = the opposite of agentic.

B.why: The marked answer. A decision tree is a workflow, not an agent. Trap for people who like determinism.

C.why: "Orchestration layer routes automatically" — again, that's a pipeline, not an agent.

D.why: Tool result → conversation → model reasons → next action. That's the definition.

sig: metadata was lost during the summarization
23.cue: Metadata dies in prose summaries → carry it as STRUCTURED data.

A.why: Re-searching to guess sources after the fact = expensive archaeology.

B.why: Inline citations in prose can work but get mangled/dropped in the next summarization.

C.why: Structured output: summary here, source metadata there. Nothing can silently vanish.

D.why: "Skip summarization, pass everything" — the extreme answer. Context bomb.

24.cue: Tell the agent what KIND of error it got: structured error + retryable flag.

A.why: retryable:false + friendly explanation fixes retries AND response quality — both asks in the stem.

B.why: Teaching the model to parse error prose = coaching around a fixable interface.

C.why: Handles retries at the tool level, but does nothing for customer-facing quality (half the ask).

D.why: A mandatory pre-check tool adds a call to every refund to dodge fixing the error format.

25.cue: Tool descriptions ARE the interface. Vague description = ignored tool.

A.why: Removing Write breaks everything else Write is for.

B.why: Explain when each tool beats sed, plus inputs/outputs. The model picks tools by their descriptions.

C.why: External intent-classifier routing = bolt-on infrastructure for a documentation problem.

D.why: "Accept it" is never the certification answer.

26.cue: The formats aren't the bug — flattening them is. Render each type as itself.

A.why: All-prose destroys the financial tables.

B.why: A "common intermediate representation" is the same flattening with extra steps.

C.why: Teach synthesis to render tables as tables, prose as prose. Preserve each format's strength.

D.why: All-JSON destroys the news narrative. Mirror image of A.

sig: reference "typical rendering patterns" rather than the specific
27.cue: Generic answers = context rot. Summarize what's good, spawn fresh for the new task.

A.why: /clear nukes the rendering knowledge the physics task NEEDS (integration!).

B.why: Distill rendering findings → seed a fresh sub-agent. Keeps signal, sheds rot.

C.why: Independent sub-agent works, but "manually synthesize" in a rotted main context is the weak link.

D.why: The context is already degrading — pushing harder into it makes it worse.

28.cue: Math: batch interval + 24h processing ≤ 30h SLA → interval ≤ 6h.

A.why: Real-time forfeits the 50% discount the stem says you want.

B.why: Worst case = 6h wait + 24h processing = 30h. Largest interval that still meets SLA = fewest batches.

C.why: Also meets SLA (28h worst case) with margin — defensible, but B is the boundary answer exams want.

D.why: End-of-day batch: a morning doc waits ~+24h before a 24h window. Blows the SLA.

sig: loses track of which sources support which conclusions when combining
29.cue: Same as Q23: claim→source as structured data that MUST survive the merge.

A.why: A log-mining "citation-resolution agent" = forensic bolt-on.

B.why: Your marked answer — agreed. Structured claim-source mappings, preserved through synthesis.

C.why: Text prefixes get paraphrased away by the next LLM step. Fragile.

D.why: Semantic-similarity guessing = reconstructing what you should never have lost.

sig: it generates messages like "I'll ask the web search agent
30.cue: Talks about delegating but can't = missing the Task tool permission.

A.why: Context forwarding issues would show garbled subagent runs — here NOTHING runs.

B.why: It clearly knows about the subagents — it names them.

C.why: Truncation would throw errors. Logs show none.

D.why: Reason-but-no-action + silent = the Task tool isn't in allowedTools. It literally cannot pull the trigger.

31.cue: Unknown path → adaptive investigation. Plans made blind are worthless.

A.why: "Executing each step regardless of intermediate findings" — the stem mocks itself.

B.why: Generate next steps from what each step reveals. Debugging IS adaptive search.

C.why: Parallel layer-agents burn effort on 3 innocent layers; error tracing is sequential by nature.

D.why: A "comprehensive plan before any exploration" of 200+ unknown files = fiction.

32.cue: Compact before you accumulate: keep the return-relevant fields, drop the rest.

A.why: Prose summaries work but are lossier/less precise than field extraction.

B.why: Keep items, dates, return window, status; cut the other 35 fields. Precise compaction.

C.why: A vector DB for a support chat = infrastructure cosplay.

D.why: Context is already majority tool-output and two more orders are coming. Doing nothing = rot.

sig: cannot be left to model discretion
33.cue: "GUARANTEED compliance" = code, not prompts. Hook intercepts the call.

A.why: LOUDER prompt is still a prompt — you already know prompts fail 3% of the time.

B.why: Tool-side rejection genuinely blocks it, but the escalation still depends on the model reacting well.

C.why: Hook: deterministic intercept ≥$500 → block + escalate. 0% is only achievable in code.

D.why: Few-shot = more prompting. Same class of fix that already failed.

34.cue: Format inconsistency → few-shot with a standardized target format.

A.why: Temp 0 makes it consistently pick SOMETHING — not consistently the right format.

B.why: Not a capability gap; the model was never shown the desired format.

C.why: Required-field forcing doesn't standardize format and invites guessing.

D.why: 2-3 input→output pairs showing the exact materials format. Demonstrate, don't hope.

sig: reports "insufficient results" rather than trying alternative
35.cue: Over-scripted subagent → give goals + quality criteria, not procedures.

A.why: Classifying into two instruction styles = managing the symptom with more machinery.

B.why: Fallback directives = MORE script on top of too much script.

C.why: Right direction, too far — "research X" with zero criteria loses quality control.

D.why: Your marked answer — agreed. Goals + criteria (coverage, diversity, recency); agent owns the how.

sig: wrapper modules that rename the function
calculateTax in the library becomes computeOrderTax
36.cue: The stem TELLS you names differ → enumerate all names first, then grep each.

A.why: Import-based reading of every importer = huge manual sweep, still miss re-exports.

B.why: Docs are stale fiction in legacy codebases.

C.why: Find every exposed alias, grep each one. Directly answers the trap in the stem.

D.why: Grep for the original name misses computeOrderTax — the stem's whole point.

sig: asks them to provide their name again
as if the earlier exchange never happened
37.cue: Claude API is STATELESS. Amnesia = you didn't send the history back.

A.why: No prompt instruction creates memory — memory is the transcript you send.

B.why: Tools can't clear model state; there is no server-side model state.

C.why: Conversation history isn't being passed in subsequent requests. The stateless-API classic.

D.why: "Two-turn default memory" is invented. Pure myth option.

sig: hasn't yet located all test files
38.cue: Big investigation + context filling → subagents do the reading, main agent keeps the map.

A.why: Scratchpad + selective re-read is legit, but /clear drops mid-flight reasoning; subagents scale better for 45 files.

B.why: Subagents explore ("find test files", "trace refund flow") and return findings; main context stays lean.

C.why: A summary as SOLE reference = everything not in it is gone forever.

D.why: Grep-only trades away the understanding the task requires.

39.cue: Q7's twin: shared analysis + two independent branches = fork_session.

A.why: Fork yesterday's session twice; each branch explores one approach with full context.

B.why: "Manually recreating the original context" — the stem confesses the waste.

C.why: Sequential = approach 2 biased by approach 1's proposals.

D.why: Fresh sessions from a summary = discount context for a decision that deserves full context.

40.cue: Open-ended real world vs. closed enum → "other" + detail field.

A.why: Force-mapping a warehouse to "house" = confidently wrong data.

B.why: Enum whack-a-mole; the stem says new types keep coming. Never ends.

C.why: Free-form works but you lose validation on the 90% that ARE the four types.

D.why: Enum keeps validation for common types; "other"+detail absorbs the long tail. Long-term stable.

sig: synthesized into a single confident statement (losing nuance)
41.cue: Uncertainty isn't noise to filter — it's content to PRESERVE and present.

A.why: Confidence filtering deletes legitimately uncertain findings.

B.why: The marked answer. Two-source corroboration discards valid single-source data AND still doesn't say how to present disagreement.

C.why: Fake-precision probability scores from vibes, then averaging $50B with $35B = mush.

D.why: Report structure: established vs. contested, keep each source's own characterization. Handles BOTH failure modes in the stem.

42.cue: Q24's twin. The tool KNOWS the error type — just say it. Structured error metadata.

A.why: Blanket retries at server level retry permission errors too. Wrong layer.

B.why: The marked answer. A whole extra tool call to analyze an error the first tool could have just... described.

C.why: Few-shot to interpret "Operation failed"? There's nothing IN it to interpret.

D.why: errorCategory + isRetryable + description at the source. One field fixes all three bad behaviors.

sig: cannot complete the task because no research findings were provided
43.cue: Q2's twin. Empty-handed subagent = coordinator didn't pass the outputs.

A.why: Coordinator must put prior outputs in the synthesis prompt. Isolation means nothing arrives by magic.

B.why: Agents can't fetch each other's histories — isolated.

C.why: It said NO findings, not truncated findings.

D.why: "Shared API connection" for auto context sharing = not a thing.

sig: preserving the coordinator's ability to monitor
44.cue: Independent items + must stay debuggable → coordinator-spawned parallel subagents.

A.why: Recursive hierarchy = the coordinator can't see what grandchildren are doing.

B.why: A message queue is real infra with real ops burden — and opaque to the coordinator.

C.why: Coordinator fans out precedent subsets in parallel, aggregates. Fast AND visible.

D.why: Self-spawning subagents = monitoring blind spot; stem explicitly demands monitorability.

sig: coordinator already has these findings in its context
45.cue: Don't hire a subagent to read you your own notes.

A.why: Caching cuts cost of the transfer — but the transfer itself is the pointless part.

B.why: Coordinator summarizes from its own context. Zero handoff, instant.

C.why: Pre-generating summaries at every granularity = speculative work forever.

D.why: On-demand back-and-forth ADDS round trips to a latency problem.

46.cue: Q25's twin — the stem SHOWS you the two descriptions side by side. Fix the thin one.

A.why: Splitting tools with equally thin descriptions = three ignored tools instead of one.

B.why: Routing rules in the prompt can work but are per-case patching; the description gap stays.

C.why: Removing Grep breaks every non-dependency search.

D.why: Describe what it actually returns (graph, transitive deps, cycles). Model picks tools by description quality.

47.cue: Escalation = handoff. Package what you learned, structured.

A.why: DB-persist + reference ID is heavier machinery; fine, but the structured handoff is the core move.

B.why: Original message only = the human re-does the whole investigation.

C.why: Customer details + order info + identified issue → escalate. Human starts where the agent stopped.

D.why: Attempting an unauthorized refund to see if it bounces = yikes.

48.cue: Multiple issues to revisit → persist STRUCTURED per-issue facts, not vibes.

A.why: Sliding 30-turn window silently drops the refund (turns 1-15) — the exact thing asked about.

B.why: Narrative summaries keep the gist but smear the order IDs/amounts you'll need verbatim.

C.why: Structured issue data (IDs, amounts, statuses) persisted per issue. Any issue is re-addressable.

D.why: Re-fetching gets order state, but not what was SAID/decided in the conversation.

sig: I want to talk to a real person NOW
has not yet called any tools
49.cue: Explicit human demand + repeated failures → escalate. Don't negotiate.

A.why: "One more question" is exactly what they just said is killing them.

B.why: Delaying escalation to run lookups = stalling with extra steps.

C.why: Making them ASK TWICE for a human = the anti-pattern by name.

D.why: Twice explained + explicit demand = escalate now, with history attached. (Contrast Q4: there the fix was instant, so offering choice made sense.)

sig: won't have access to your conversation transcript
50.cue: Q47's twin, harder cutoff: structured summary — ID, root cause, amount, recommendation.

A.why: Verbatim complaint + raw excerpts = evidence without a diagnosis. Human still assembles the story.

B.why: Diagnosis + amount only — no customer ID, human can't even find the account.

C.why: Customer ID + root cause + amount + recommended action. Everything needed, nothing extra.

D.why: 25+ turns of transcript they "won't have access to" — and wouldn't want.

sig: cannot find unique text to match
insert a new helper function into the middle
51.cue: Edit's anchor fails → Read → modify → Write the whole file.

A.why: 30+ line old_string = one whitespace drift from failing again. Fragile.

B.why: Append to the END when the stem says it goes in the MIDDLE.

C.why: Read the file, insert at the right spot, Write it back. Boring and bulletproof.

D.why: replace_all on a COMMON pattern = the function inserted N times.

sig: inconsistent answers about code structure it discussed earlier
52.cue: Long-session drift → externalize findings to a scratchpad file.

A.why: Bigger context delays the rot; the findings still degrade in-window.

B.why: Scratchpad file = durable memory outside the context window. Re-read beats recall.

C.why: Pre-summarizing ALL files before knowing what matters = huge waste, thin understanding.

D.why: Clearing every 15 min GUARANTEES the amnesia engineers are complaining about.

sig: most reliably identify cases that genuinely require human intervention
53.cue: Criteria for model judgment > mechanical triggers. (Explicit request / policy exception / stuck.)

A.why: Three failed calls = mechanical; escalates transient blips, misses zero-tool-call cases like Q49.

B.why: A rules engine "removing model judgment" can't enumerate the real world.

C.why: Clear criteria, model applies judgment: user asks, policy exception, no progress. Covers what matters.

D.why: Counting exclamation marks!!! is not understanding frustration.

sig: correct pattern for communicating these errors
54.cue: Pure recall: MCP errors = isError:true + message in content.

A.why: The MCP spec pattern: result with isError flag set, error text in content. The agent sees it and adapts.

B.why: Exceptions die in the framework — the MODEL never learns what happened.

C.why: Success-wrapped errors ("status" field) = agent thinks it worked.

D.why: Empty result "to avoid confusing the model" confuses it maximally.

55.cue: Fix ONLY the 300, and fix the ACTUAL error (input too long → chunk).

A.why: Resubmitting all 10,000 to fix 300 = paying 33x. And on a pricier tier.

B.why: custom_id gives you the exact 300; chunking fixes input-too-long specifically.

C.why: max_tokens caps OUTPUT. The error is INPUT length. Doesn't touch the problem.

D.why: Caching discounts a full reprocess that shouldn't happen at all.

56.cue: Entry points → follow the flow. Auth is a FLOW; trace it, don't bulk-read.

A.why: Grep entry points, read, follow imports/calls. Incremental, targeted, context-friendly — and auth flow crosses services as ONE thread.

B.why: CLAUDE.md first is fine, but dumping file-picking on the new engineer defeats the purpose.

C.why: Parallel subagents per service is defensible at 800 files — but each sees a fragment of a flow that only makes sense end-to-end.

D.why: Reading every file containing "token" in 800+ files = context massacre.

sig: agent often references the outdated data
even after subsequent fresh tool calls
57.cue: Stale results poison even fresh ones → new session + structured summary + fresh calls.

A.why: Stripping tool_results helps, but orphaned assistant turns still narrate the stale data ("your refund is pending...").

B.why: The stem already told you instructions lose to stale context ("even after fresh calls").

C.why: Auto re-calling everything doesn't remove the stale copies — the confusion source stays in context.

D.why: Clean context: summary of what happened (issue, actions, status) + fresh tool calls. Stale data physically can't be quoted.

sig: minimize API costs while meeting latency
58.cue: Two SLAs = two paths. Batch the slow, real-time the urgent.

A.why: Route by urgency: 50% savings on the bulk, 30-min alerts still guaranteed. The stem is begging for a split.

B.why: Batch can take 24h; "immediately process when results arrive" can't rescue a 30-MINUTE alert.

C.why: All real-time = paying double on the archive pile for no reason.

D.why: Hourly batch + 24h window already blows 30 minutes before "expedited handling" begins.

sig: doesn't match the extracted grand total
OCR errors in the source document
59.cue: Can't know which side is wrong → surface BOTH numbers, flag mismatches for humans.

A.why: A second model guessing which value is "most likely correct" for ACCOUNTING data = no.

B.why: Few-shot can nudge the model, but it can't fix OCR errors in the source (half the causes).

C.why: calculated_total vs stated_total: mismatch becomes a visible flag, humans review only the 18%. Built-in audit.

D.why: Auto-adjusting line items to force the math = silently fabricating financial records. Career-ending answer.

sig: semantic errors that pass JSON schema validation
60.cue: Targeted review beats random → calibrated confidence routes reviewers to the risky 20%.

A.why: Random sampling measures the error rate but catches only ~20% of errors. Baseline, not allocation.

B.why: Formatting anomalies ≠ semantic errors; the stem's example error needs no weird layout.

C.why: Empty/not-found fields are the HONEST cases; the bug is confidently-wrong FILLED fields.

D.why: Confidence scores calibrated on labeled data → review the least-confident slice. Attention goes where errors live.
